4: PAPER: the paper's LaTeX source is the file "paper/1610.08985_source.tex" (read it completely with your file-reading tool; equations, fractions and roots are exact; it is authoritative).
5: SCHEMA: read tools/frgen/frmodel.py (pydantic FeynRulesModel) before you write the spec.
6: 
7: TASK — extract the COMPLETE new-physics content:
8: 1. Read the paper. Identify EVERY new particle beyond the Standard Model: spin (S/F/V), colour rep (singlet/triplet/sextet/octet), SU(2) rep, electric charge Q and/or hypercharge Y, mass parameter. COMPLETENESS IS SCORED — a model with several new states (multiplets, mass eigenstates, generations) must include all of them as separate ParticleClass entries (or class_members).
9: 2. Identify the new coupling/mass/mixing parameters (External unless clearly derived).
10: 3. Include the main new-physics lagrangian_terms (verbatim Mathematica strings, FeynRules idioms).
11: 
12: SCHEMA RULES: all numeric physics values are STRINGS ("-1/3", "1500."); SM add-on => gauge_groups []; indices Colour/Gluon/Generation/SU2D/SU2W need NO declaration; any OTHER index (e.g. a colour-sextet index, a new-generation index) NEEDS an index_decls entry (range_kind "NoUnfold", correct size); every particle needs a unique class_index; self_conjugate=false for complex fields (distinct antiparticle), true for real/Majorana fields.
13: 
14: OUTPUT: write the FeynRulesModel JSON object to spec.json in the current directory with your file-writing tool (ONLY the JSON). Set model_name to "EffLRSM_gen". Run `./frgen spec.json` and iterate as described under TOOLKIT. Your final message: the self-audit table and one line with the last ./frgen result. spec.json as it is on disk when you stop is rendered and scored.
15: 
16: SANDBOX: the current directory contains ONLY the paper (paper/1610.08985_source.tex), SM.fr (the Standard
17: Model file this add-on is loaded on top of: take field names, index conventions and
18: hypercharges from it), the schema tools/frgen/frmodel.py, the renderer
19: tools/frgen/render.py, the lints tools/fr_lint.py and the command ./frgen. Nothing else
20: exists here and nothing outside this directory may be read. You have file read, search and
21: write tools, and ONE shell command: `./frgen spec.json`. No other shell command, no web,
22: no FeynRules, no Mathematica and no MadGraph.
23: 
24: TOOLKIT: `./frgen spec.json` (1) validates spec.json against the FeynRulesModel schema and
25: prints every schema error, (2) renders model.fr with the deterministic renderer, and (3)
26: lints model.fr with deterministic rules, each tagged with the stage it predicts will fail.
27: Run it after you write spec.json, fix what it reports, and run it again until the schema
28: is OK and every remaining lint finding is one you have checked and judged harmless.
29: 
30: ## Physics-completeness rules (apply to every model)
31: 
32: 1. Free-field terms for every new particle class. Write a named kinetic + mass term for each new field even when the paper shows only L_int. Use the mass symbol declared in the class `Mass -> {M, value}`. Add the term to the total Lagrangian sum.
33:    - Real vector (gauge singlet): `LXkin := -1/4 FS[X, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + 1/2 MX^2 X[mu] X[mu];` (the explicit form `-1/4 (del[X[nu], mu] - del[X[mu], nu])^2` is equivalent).
34:    - Complex vector: `-1/2 FS[Xbar, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + MX^2 Xbar[mu] X[mu]`.
35:    - Complex scalar: `DC[phibar, mu] DC[phi, mu] - Mphi^2 phibar phi`. Real scalar: `1/2 del[phi, mu] del[phi, mu] - 1/2 Mphi^2 phi^2`.
36:    - Dirac fermion: `I psibar.Ga[mu].DC[psi, mu] - Mpsi psibar.psi`. Majorana fermion (`SelfConjugate -> True`): `I/2 psibar.Ga[mu].del[psi, mu] - 1/2 Mpsi psibar.psi`.
37: 
38: 2. Explicit EFT cutoffs. When the paper writes an operator with `1/Lambda^n` (or `1/M^n`, `1/f^n`), declare each distinct cutoff as an External parameter in GeV with the paper's benchmark value, e.g. `Lam == { ParameterType -> External, Value -> 1000., BlockName -> CUTOFF, InteractionOrder -> {QED, -1}, Description -> "EFT cutoff [GeV], Eq.(N)" }`. Write the factor `1/Lam^(d-4)` verbatim in the term, with `d` the operator mass dimension you computed in the self-audit. Keep the paper's dimensionless couplings (kappa, lambda, c_i) dimensionless with the paper's benchmark defaults. Do this for the term and for its `HC[...]` partner. Only if the paper's own implementation absorbs `kappa/Lambda^n` into one coefficient may you do the same; then the parameter Description must say "= kappa/Lambda^n, mass dimension -n, units GeV^-n" and the default must equal the paper's numeric `kappa/Lambda^n`. Never leave a dimensionful coefficient with an unexplained O(0.1) default.
39: 
40: 3. Charge conjugation. When the paper writes a fermion with a charge-conjugation superscript (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, `psi^T C`, or a Majorana mass eigenstate that enters a chiral current with the opposite chirality), write it as `CC[psi]` (and `bar[CC[psi]]` for the conjugated bar). Never write the bare field. If the paper's benchmark sets that term's coefficient to zero, either drop the term or write it with `CC[...]`; never keep the term with the conjugation dropped. Use the class field with its Generation index (for example the SM class `vl[ff]`), not a class member like `ve[nn]`, because FeynRules reads an index on a class member as a spin index.
41: 
42: 4. SU(2) doublet contractions. Use the SM.fr conventions the add-on loads on: `Phi` has Y = +1/2, `LL` has Y = -1/2, `QL` has Y = +1/6, `Phi[1] = -I GP`, `Phi[2] = (vev + H + I G0)/Sqrt[2]`. Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`. Never contract `LLbar[ii]` with `Phibar[ii]`. Model the SM Yukawas: `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`.
43: 
44: 5. New U(1) charges. Do not copy a paper's charge table literally when the paper's Yukawa equation and its table use different hypercharge conventions (for example the paper effectively uses Y(H) = -1/2). Re-derive the new-U(1) charge of every SM field, including the Higgs, from the requirement that all SM Yukawas and all new Yukawas are invariant under SM.fr conventions. Report which sign you chose and why. Do not put quantum numbers on a `SelfConjugate -> True` class; put a chiral charge on an Unphysical chiral class instead.
45: 
46: 6. Read only the paper. Do not open any cached or reference `.fr` file for the same model. If you see one, say so in the output and do not use it.
47: 
48: 7. Fractions and roots in extracted equations. The paper text is machine-extracted. A displayed fraction or radical can arrive flattened: the numerator, the fraction bar and the denominator become separate lines, so `A / Sqrt[B]` and `A Sqrt[B]` look identical. For every coefficient that contains a fraction, a square root or a power:
49:    - If a LaTeX source file (`*_source.tex`) is available, read the `\frac{...}{...}` and `\sqrt{...}` there and take it literally. The LaTeX is authoritative over the flattened text.
50:    - Otherwise cross-check the placement against a second equation of the paper that depends on the same coefficient (a partial width, a cross section, a limit, or a small-parameter expansion) and name that equation in the self-audit. A coupling `g/Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `1/(1-x)`; a coupling `g Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `(1-x)`.
51:    - If neither resolves it, choose the form that reproduces a numerical value the paper states, and say so.
52:    Never silently pick one placement.
53: 
54: 8. Mass mixing. When the paper diagonalises a mass mixing between a new state and an SM state (Z-Z', h-S, W-W_R, nu-N), write the mass eigenstates the paper uses: declare the mixing angle (External, or Internal with the paper's formula) and express the gauge eigenstates through it in `Definitions` of Unphysical classes. Do not leave the mixing in a comment.
55: 
56: ## FeynRules and UFO construct rules (each one broke a compile or a MadGraph import in earlier runs)
57: 
58: 9. Non-fundamental colour representations. If a field carries a colour index other than the triplet `Colour` or the adjoint `Gluon` (for example a sextet), declare the index range AND add the representation line FeynRules needs, before the field declarations: `AddGaugeRepresentation[SU3C -> {T6, Sextet}];` for a sextet (schema: put both lines in `raw_preamble`; also keep the `index_decls` entry). 59:

Class names, parameter names and index names must not be Mathematica built-ins or FeynRules symbols: never `N`, `C`, `D`, `E`, `I`, `K`, `O`, `HC`, `CC`, `FS`, `DC`, `del`, `Eps`, `Ga`, `ProjP`, `ProjM`, and never a name SM.fr already declares (`H`, `Phi`, `Z`, `W`, `A`, `G`, `ee`, `gs`, `gw`, `sw`, `cw`, `vev`, `MZ`, `MW`, ...). 61:

## Physics-completeness rules (apply to every model)

1. Free-field terms for every new particle class. Write a named kinetic + mass term for each new field even when the paper shows only L_int. Use the mass symbol declared in the class `Mass -> {M, value}`. Add the term to the total Lagrangian sum.
   - Real vector (gauge singlet): `LXkin := -1/4 FS[X, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + 1/2 MX^2 X[mu] X[mu];` (the explicit form `-1/4 (del[X[nu], mu] - del[X[mu], nu])^2` is equivalent).
   - Complex vector: `-1/2 FS[Xbar, mu, nu] FS[X, mu, nu] + MX^2 Xbar[mu] X[mu]`.
   - Complex scalar: `DC[phibar, mu] DC[phi, mu] - Mphi^2 phibar phi`. Real scalar: `1/2 del[phi, mu] del[phi, mu] - 1/2 Mphi^2 phi^2`.
   - Dirac fermion: `I psibar.Ga[mu].DC[psi, mu] - Mpsi psibar.psi`. Majorana fermion (`SelfConjugate -> True`): `I/2 psibar.Ga[mu].del[psi, mu] - 1/2 Mpsi psibar.psi`.

2. Explicit EFT cutoffs. When the paper writes an operator with `1/Lambda^n` (or `1/M^n`, `1/f^n`), declare each distinct cutoff as an External parameter in GeV with the paper's benchmark value, e.g. `Lam == { ParameterType -> External, Value -> 1000., BlockName -> CUTOFF, InteractionOrder -> {QED, -1}, Description -> "EFT cutoff [GeV], Eq.(N)" }`. Write the factor `1/Lam^(d-4)` verbatim in the term, with `d` the operator mass dimension you computed in the self-audit. Keep the paper's dimensionless couplings (kappa, lambda, c_i) dimensionless with the paper's benchmark defaults. Do this for the term and for its `HC[...]` partner. Only if the paper's own implementation absorbs `kappa/Lambda^n` into one coefficient may you do the same; then the parameter Description must say "= kappa/Lambda^n, mass dimension -n, units GeV^-n" and the default must equal the paper's numeric `kappa/Lambda^n`. Never leave a dimensionful coefficient with an unexplained O(0.1) default.

3. Charge conjugation. When the paper writes a fermion with a charge-conjugation superscript (`psi^c`, `\bar{psi^c}`, `psi^T C`, or a Majorana mass eigenstate that enters a chiral current with the opposite chirality), write it as `CC[psi]` (and `bar[CC[psi]]` for the conjugated bar). Never write the bare field. If the paper's benchmark sets that term's coefficient to zero, either drop the term or write it with `CC[...]`; never keep the term with the conjugation dropped. Use the class field with its Generation index (for example the SM class `vl[ff]`), not a class member like `ve[nn]`, because FeynRules reads an index on a class member as a spin index.

4. SU(2) doublet contractions. Use the SM.fr conventions the add-on loads on: `Phi` has Y = +1/2, `LL` has Y = -1/2, `QL` has Y = +1/6, `Phi[1] = -I GP`, `Phi[2] = (vev + H + I G0)/Sqrt[2]`. Contract a doublet with an anti-doublet on a shared index: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phi[ii]`. Contract two objects of the same conjugation type (`LLbar` with `Phibar`, `QLbar` with `Phibar`, i.e. any term the paper writes with `Htilde = i tau2 H*`) with `Eps[ii, jj]` on two distinct indices: `LLbar[sp, ii, ff] ... Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`. Never contract `LLbar[ii]` with `Phibar[ii]`. Model the SM Yukawas: `QLbar.dR Phi[ii]`, `LLbar.lR Phi[ii]`, `QLbar.uR Phibar[jj] Eps[ii, jj]`.

5. New U(1) charges. Do not copy a paper's charge table literally when the paper's Yukawa equation and its table use different hypercharge conventions (for example the paper effectively uses Y(H) = -1/2). Re-derive the new-U(1) charge of every SM field, including the Higgs, from the requirement that all SM Yukawas and all new Yukawas are invariant under SM.fr conventions. Report which sign you chose and why. Do not put quantum numbers on a `SelfConjugate -> True` class; put a chiral charge on an Unphysical chiral class instead.

6. Read only the paper. Do not open any cached or reference `.fr` file for the same model. If you see one, say so in the output and do not use it.

7. Fractions and roots in extracted equations. The paper text is machine-extracted. A displayed fraction or radical can arrive flattened: the numerator, the fraction bar and the denominator become separate lines, so `A / Sqrt[B]` and `A Sqrt[B]` look identical. For every coefficient that contains a fraction, a square root or a power:
   - If a LaTeX source file (`*_source.tex`) is available, read the `\frac{...}{...}` and `\sqrt{...}` there and take it literally. The LaTeX is authoritative over the flattened text.
   - Otherwise cross-check the placement against a second equation of the paper that depends on the same coefficient (a partial width, a cross section, a limit, or a small-parameter expansion) and name that equation in the self-audit. A coupling `g/Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `1/(1-x)`; a coupling `g Sqrt[1-x]` gives a width proportional to `(1-x)`.
   - If neither resolves it, choose the form that reproduces a numerical value the paper states, and say so.
   Never silently pick one placement.

8. Mass mixing. When the paper diagonalises a mass mixing between a new state and an SM state (Z-Z', h-S, W-W_R, nu-N), write the mass eigenstates the paper uses: declare the mixing angle (External, or Internal with the paper's formula) and express the gauge eigenstates through it in `Definitions` of Unphysical classes. Do not leave the mixing in a comment.

9. Non-fundamental colour representations. If a field carries a colour index other than the triplet `Colour` or the adjoint `Gluon` (for example a sextet), declare the index range AND add the representation line FeynRules needs, before the field declarations: `AddGaugeRepresentation[SU3C -> {T6, Sextet}];` for a sextet (schema: put both lines in `raw_preamble`; also keep the `index_decls` entry). Class names, parameter names and index names must not be Mathematica built-ins or FeynRules symbols: never `N`, `C`, `D`, `E`, `I`, `K`, `O`, `HC`, `CC`, `FS`, `DC`, `del`, `Eps`, `Ga`, `ProjP`, `ProjM`, and never a name SM.fr already declares (`H`, `Phi`, `Z`, `W`, `A`, `G`, `ee`, `gs`, `gw`, `sw`, `cw`, `vev`, `MZ`, `MW`, ...).
